career_spells.employer: Private legal practices, including Conaghan Lawyers Pty Ltd (separate practice timelines unresolved)
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen extract records solicitor work from 2001 to 2019. Secondary material says Conaghan established his own criminal-defence practice, and a public professional-profile result names Conaghan Lawyers. ABN Lookup records the Australian private company as active from 6 July 2001. The corporate registration date does not prove Conaghan's exact work start; exact cessation, hours, ownership period, leave and campaign overlap remain unresolved. Public3December2014 professional introduction confirms principal role in Port Macquarie.2019 parliamentary declaration identifies retained shareholding/directorship and calls law-firm income passive; do not extend active legal employment merely because company and income continued. Follow-up profiles identify three businesses/practices and defence, immigration and commercial litigation. The official2001–2019 interval is solicitor work overall, not proof of continuous employment at this one company; retain aggregate pending employer-by-employer disaggregation. Second follow-up2October2026 identifies nested practice intervals: Conaghan Hunter Solicitors August2005–December2010 and Conaghan Lawyers December2010–May2019. Aggregate retained to cover unresolved earlier2001–2005 work; no double counting. Public profile also describes sole-practitioner duties, but employer/date association not exposed sufficiently to assign another bounded spell.
career_spells.counting_note: Private control and self-employment are supported, but year-only work boundaries and unproven substantive full-time status prevent an exact headline duration.

research_notes: The frozen official extract supplies a continuous year-level occupation sequence from 1990 to parliamentary entry but not exact transitions or working hours.
The private company's registration date corroborates legal-entity existence and control, not the exact first day of Conaghan's work.
Police ranks and professional titles are not treated as proof of substantive full-time status.
Council service overlapped private legal practice and is excluded rather than double-counted.

Systematic follow-up2026-10-01 added omitted pool-cleaning job, explicit full-time evidence limited to undercover subspell, concurrent law study, principal-lawyer2014 observation and retained company governance/passive income2019.

Full-time status comes from publicly indexed first-person interview, supported by publisher caption, not from police rank. Direct social-source fetches throttled; no bypass/retry. Podcast listing supplies further review lead at2:28:46, not reviewed full audio. Need exact assignment dates before any duration calculation.

First speech’s two undercover years and four prosecution years are narrative durations only. Birth date/age13/age25 not used to manufacture employment dates. Undercover spell is nested; union overlapping public intervals if eventually countable.

Searched parliamentary first speech and register, public professional profiles, law-practice site, undergraduate leads and council history. APH first-speech direct403 but official indexed content available; personal site verification screen and law-firm site unavailable. No exact law-study/appointment/hours evidence located. Further public police histories, alumni records, court appearances and practice history remain leads.

New speaker and charity participant biographies identify three legal businesses/practices, so the2001–2019 solicitor spell is relabelled as overall private practice rather than attributing every year to Conaghan Lawyers. Conaghan Hunter Lawyers appears as a court-listing lead, but no personal employment link or separate term yet established. ABR historical-name pages inaccessible. Professional Planner says five Drug Enforcement years; first speech distinguishes two undercover years from later investigation, and frozen detective interval1993–1997 is retained pending reconciliation.

Second follow-up2October2026 materially disaggregates two legal practices using public professional-profile index: Conaghan Hunter August2005–December2010 and Conaghan Lawyers December2010–May2019. These components remain nested in overall2001–2019 solicitor interval. Added omitted College of Law diploma study without inferred dates.

Earlier2001–2005 practice identity/terms, law-school dates and undercover assignment boundaries remain unresolved. UK civil servant, US lawyer and Macquarie geologist namesakes excluded. Public index used without authenticated profile or direct-access retry. May2019 cessation is month precision only and does not settle campaign leave, passive-income transition day or hours.

Follow-up3October2026 tested earlier-practice identity via Conaghan Legal, sole-practitioner and2001–2005 searches on two public search engines. ABR80 527 846 642 names Patrick Conaghan, individual/sole trader, active2003–2009 and from2011; Conaghan Legal trading name from18November2003 and separately registered business name17February2004–19May2010. Identity link to this member remains unconfirmed; locality/name similarity is not sufficient. These registration milestones do not establish personal employment boundaries, continuity or hours. No new employer/date/full-time fact adopted. Public professional-profile index again exposed police sequence but not earlier sole-practice dates; existing dates retained. US and unrelated Australian namesakes excluded. Next useful avenue is a historical firm biography or professional directory explicitly pairing this member with Conaghan Legal; do not repeat broad name searches.
